displayOrder.name: Category Workspace
displayOrder.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a realistic, production-quality PokeTaskBar macOS desktop SETTINGS page with clear hierarchy, precise typography and purposeful spacing.
References: attached image 1 is the approved Today window shell, image 2 is the approved line-free Usage provider layout, image 3 is the existing small Settings screen showing real controls. Match the first two for visual language; use the third only to ground Settings functionality. This is a spacious main app window, not the small menu panel.
Target 1488 x 1056 landscape, straight-on complete native macOS window, matching reference proportions. Current date Friday 18 September 2026, but no date is needed on Settings. No surrounding browser, presentation title, option number, annotations or oversized poster title.
Keep the approved expanded main left navigation about240px wide: PokeTaskBar identity, Cody with chevron, Search, Today, Focus, Issues, Projects, Initiatives, Collection, Usage, Settings anchored near bottom. Settings selected using a quiet neutral row fill. Native red/yellow/green traffic lights, back/forward arrows, compact Settings page tab, sidebar collapse/reopen controls. Sidebars are independently collapsible and resizable; all guides hidden at rest.
Continuous flat #EFF0F2 shell, pale #F8F8FA main content canvas inset on ALL edges with rounded corners and visible lower corners. White rounded content surfaces only for meaningful groups. Ink#242528, metadata#73757B, restrained blue toggles and focus, neutral selections. SF Pro-like type14-16pt body,28-32pt main headings. Body copy readable, consistent modest outline icons.
CRITICAL: NO permanent vertical divider beside navigation, NO line under account identity, NO major horizontal section rules, NO vertical separators between columns, NO resize grip dots. Use open gutters, whitespace and tonal rounded surfaces. Avoid card outlines and avoid boxing individual settings rows. No glass, gradients, glow, heavy shadows, marketing art, chart, Pokémon hero or scores on Settings.
Goal: make app preferences easy to find and adjust, using the actual existing settings. Focus this viewport on General preferences, with other categories reachable without showing every control.
The six General controls and mock values are: Language = English dropdown; Representative Pokémon = Follow current dropdown (choosing a specific representative routes into Collection); Refresh interval = 2 min dropdown; Animation quality = Balanced dropdown with quiet explanation 'Smoother animation uses more battery'; Limit display = Used / Remaining segmented control with Remaining selected; Launch at login = On switch. These values are illustrative, not a readout of actual preferences.
Existing other groups available through navigation/disclosures: Linear; Difficulty; Menu bar; Floating pet; Notifications; Updates; Data & backup; Advanced; About & support. You may group these under broader local categories if helpful, but do not invent cloud sync, account plans, themes, notification schedules, new permission settings, delete-account or reset-data actions.
Menu bar existing toggles include tokens, estimated cost, limit percentage, score, Linear issue count. Floating pet supports enable, size, bubble alerts. Notifications includes quota alerts, companion alerts, Time XP and status checks. Updates has update notifications and Check now. Data & backup has Export save / Import save. Advanced holds session-key, keychain and custom scan-path settings. Keep credentials and import actions off this General viewport.
Simple switches and dropdown changes apply directly; no global Save or Cancel bar. Credentials keep explicit Save only on their own pages. Do not imply all settings are saved successfully before an action. A proposed Find a setting control is okay as a navigational convenience. GitHub and Report a problem are existing secondary support routes.
The main canvas remains fully usable with either sidebar hidden. Right extras, if present, only hold optional explanation/support. Search/category navigation must remain in main content. Preserve generous whitespace and align every control. Avoid clipped content or UI inventories, keep six General controls as the clear focus.
Direction: Category Workspace.
Keep the optional right extras sidebar collapsed; show its reopen button in window chrome. One wide rounded pale main canvas.
At the top left of main canvas show Settings and a quiet subtitle 'Make PokeTaskBar feel right for you.' Place Find a setting at the upper right of this canvas.
Inside the canvas, establish a narrow local category list about190px at left, with NO separator stroke. Show General selected, then Linear, Difficulty, Menu bar, Floating pet, Notifications, Updates, Data & backup, Advanced, About & support as simple readable rows with small muted outline icons. This is local Settings navigation inside the main canvas, separate from the unchanged main app navigation.
To the right leave a36px open gutter and a spacious General content area. Heading General with a restrained short introduction. Show the six General controls in one white rounded grouped surface; each row around68px high with label left and its correctly sized control right, no horizontal rules. Add the Animation quality hint beneath its label only. White surface about730px wide with24px padding. Place Used/Remaining segment aligned with other dropdowns. On toggle right at last row. Give labels breathing room and preserve control alignment.
Beneath the white group, leave generous open space and two understated support links GitHub and Report a problem. No extra status cards, version claim, image preview or duplicate controls. This should most closely resemble the calm category-based settings in Linear's desktop app.

implementationNotes: The candidates organise existing settings, with General as the focused viewport. They do not approve unseen category forms or add account plans, themes or cloud features.
Find a setting is a proposed navigational convenience. Any incidental generated shortcut must be reconciled with global search rather than assigning the same shortcut to two controls.
Simple controls retain their existing immediate-apply behaviour; credential inputs keep explicit Save within their own forms.
Main navigation and optional extras remain independently collapsible and resizable without permanent section/sidebar separator strokes.
Keep all essential General controls available when optional extras collapse.
Category changes should preserve useful context; expired-session-key entry must open Advanced and focus the relevant existing field.
Existing credential storage and import/export behaviours remain unchanged by a visual selection; illustrative controls are not actual preference readings.
Settings subcategories remain accessible and use the existing controls; Collection subviews follow after approval of the main Settings layout.
